And he, with a small number of men, barely escaped,
and arrived in flight at Damascus.
And in that same year, in the latter Kanun (January),
there passed away the faithful Queen Isabel, the daughter of the great King Leo,
and wife of King Hethum, the son of Constantine,
and mother of King Leo (the second) the younger, of Cilicia.
Now the goodness, mercy, and humility of this woman, no one can recount;
for barefoot she used to walk in church courtyards,
and as long as prayers lasted,
she would not cease from weeping.
May God grant her rest with the rest of the holy women.
And at the turn of the year,
that is to say, in the year 1563,
1563 of the Greeks,
King Hethum of Cilicia went into the service of the great Möngke Khan.
Now he partook of the life-giving Mysteries on Thursday of the Mysteries (Maundy Thursday),
and set out on Friday of the Crucifixion (Good Friday).
And because he was afraid of the nobles of the Sultanate of Rum, lest they harm him by deceit,
he put out a report
that he was first sending an ambassador to the Khan,
and would receive an authorization,
and only then would he go.
And he also wrote letters to the ruler of the Sultanate of Rum to this effect.
And with this ambassador, he himself also went forth disguised in the habit of grooms, leading a horse,
dressed in soiled garments,
and riding on an ordinary mount.
And he passed through all the cities of the Sultanate of Rum, and no one recognized him,
except in Erzincan, where a certain marketplace person recognized him and said,
"This is King Hethum."
And when the ambassador heard it, he turned to the king while he was leading the horse,
struck him on his cheek, insulted him, and said,
"Yes, O fool,
were you a king here,
that they liken you to a king?"
And thus the suspicion was removed.
And in this disguise of grooms the king remained,
until he reached the border of the Iberians (Georgians),
and then he revealed himself.
Now he was outside his country at this time for nearly three and a half years,
and then he returned.
And in this same year,
which is the year six hundred and fifty of the Arabs,
after the Qurultai, that is,
the great assembly,
